figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Biosynthesis of non-native nucleotide sugars from UDP-D-Gal and UDP-D-Glc. UDP-L-Rha, UDP-D-Fuc, UDP-D-GlcA, UDP-D-Xyl, UDP-D-
Api, UDP-L-Arap, and UDP-L-Araf can be synthesized from UDP-D-Glc using de novo pathways or from free sugars using the salvage pathway. Yeast’s
native galactose metabolism (highlighted in green and boxed in orange, also known as the Leloir pathway) is the main supplier of UDP-sugars, as free
galactose can be phosphorylated by GALK and converted by GALT with UDP-D-Glc to form UDP-D-Gal and D-Glc-1-P. UDP-D-Gal is also
interconverted with UDP-D-Glc by UDP-D-Glc 4-epimerase (UGE). UDP-D-Glc can be converted to a variety of UDP-sugars using nucleotide sugar
synthases of plant origin. UDP-L-Rha is made from UDP-D-Glc using rhamnose synthase (RHM), and UDP-D-Fuc is made by UDP-glucose-4,6-
dehydratase (UG46DH) via a common keto-sugar intermediate, UDP-4-keto-6-deoxy-D-Glc, which is reduced by neomenthol dehydrogenase
(NMD). UDP-D-GlcA is synthesized from UDP-D-Glc by UDP-D-Glc 6-dehydrogenase (UGD). The C6 carboxylic acid of UDP-D-GlcA is
decarboxylated by UDP-D-Xyl synthase (UXS) to yield UDP-D-Xyl. UDP-L-Arap and UDP-L-Araf are the pyranose/furanose isomers of UDP-L-Ara.
UDP-D-Xyl 4-epimerase (UXE) synthesizes UDP-L-Arap from UDP-D-Xyl by a C4 epimerization, and UDP-L-Ara mutase (UAM) performs a
reversible ring rearrangement of UDP-L-Arap to form UDP-L-Araf. UDP-D-Api synthase (AXS) can convert UDP-D-GlcA to a mixture of UDP-D-Xyl
and UDP-D-Api. Nucleotide sugar synthesis can also be achieved using the salvage pathway (highlighted in blue), where free L-arabinose can be directly
phosphorylated by arabinose kinase (AraK) and converted to UDP-L-Arap by UDP-sugar pyrophosphorylase (USP).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Biosynthesis of UDP-Arap and UDP-Araf in engineered S. cerevisiae. (a) De novo and salvage pathways to produce UDP-L-Arap and UDP-L-
Araf. (b) Production of UDP-D-Xyl and UDP-L-Arap in strains NS-07 and NS-08 from nucleotide sugar enzymes. Both were built from NS-03, which
produces UDP-D-Xyl; NS-07 harbors AtUXE2, which can interconvert UDP-L-Arap from UDP-D-Xyl by C4-epimerization; and NS-08 similarly
harbors AtUGE3, which is also able to interconvert UDP-D-Xyl and UDP-L-Arap. (c) Production of UDP-L-Arap and (d) production of UDP-L-Araf in
yeast strains expressing salvage pathway enzymes (AtAraK and AtUSP), with 1% supplementation of arabinose as well as UDP-arabinose mutases
(UAM) from A. thaliana and O. sativa. NS-09 harbors AtAraK and AtUSP to produce UDP-L-Arap, while the other strains were constructed from NS-
09 to interconvert UDP-L-Arap to UDP-L-Araf by AtUAM1 (NS-13), OsUAM1 (NS-14), and OsUAM3 (NS-15), or OsUAM1, OsUAM2, and
OsUAM3 (NS-16). Data are mean ± s.d.; n = 3 biologically independent samples.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Tuning production of UDP-D-GlcA and UDP-D-Xyl in S. cerevisiae. (a) UDP-D-Glc is oxidized by UGD to make UDP-D-GlcA, which can be
converted to UDP-D-Xyl via UXS. UDP-D-Xyl strongly inhibits the activity of UGD. (b) Expression of AtUGD to make UDP-D-GlcA from UDP-D-Glc
in NS-01. The additional expression of AtUXS in NS-03 led to the synthesis of UDP-D-Xyl while depleting UDP-D-GlcA due to UGD inhibition by
UDP-D-Xyl. (c) Expression of AtUXS under a Gal10 promoter with AtUGD (NS-03), AtUGDA101L (NS-17), and PaUGD (NS-18) under a Gal1
promoter. (d) Expression of AtUGD under the control of a Gal1 promoter and AtUXS under the control of a Tet-On promoter (strain NS-19) with
various concentrations of doxycycline resulted in increased concentrations of UDP-D-GlcA and UDP-D-Xyl being detected in the same strain. Data are
mean ± s.d.; n = 3 biologically independent samples.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Biosynthesis of UDP-D-GlcA, UDP-D-Xyl, UDP-L-Rha, and UDP-D-Fuc. (a) Biosynthetic routes of these UDP-sugars from UDP-D-Glc.
UDP-D-Fuc and UDP-L-Rha share a UDP-4-keto-6-deoxy-D-Glc intermediate, while UDP-D-GlcA and UDP-D-Xyl are biosynthesized by the
subsequent C6 oxidation of UDP-D-Glc (AtUGD) and decarboxylation of UDP-D-GlcA (AtUXS). (b) Nucleotide sugar synthases for UDP-D-Xyl,
UDP-L-Rha, and UDP-D-Fuc biosynthesis were expressed individually in strains NS-19, NS-05, and NS-06 (see the legend for genotype) and
combinatorially in strains NS-20 to NS-23 (see legend) to study the underlying impact of coexpressing nucleotide sugar enzymes on UDP-sugar
concentrations. Strains harboring AtUXS driven by the Tet-On promoter (NS-19, NS-21, NS-22, and NS-23) were induced with 50 μg/mL
doxycycline 24 h after galactose induction. Data are mean ± s.d.; n = 3 biologically independent samples.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Time-course production of UDP-sugars in strains NS-27 and NS-28. NS-27 has all of the nucleotide sugar synthase genes to produce UDP-D-
GlcA (AtUGD), UDP-D-Xyl (AtUXS), UDP-L-Arap (AtUGE3), UDP-L-Rha (AtRHM2), and UDP-D-Fuc (SvUG46DH, SvNMD) under the control
of galactose-inducible promoters, whereas NS-28 has AtUXS driven by the Tet-On promoter and all of the other heterologous nucleotide sugar
synthases under the control of galactose-inducible promoters. UDP-D-Gal and UDP-D-Glc, which are endogenously produced in S. cerevisiae, are
outlined by a dashed orange box. In the NS-28 cultures, 50 μg/mL doxycycline was added at 24 h to induce the Tet-On promoter. Data are mean ± s.d.;
n = 3 biologically independent samples.
